question: Can a 70/20/10 error/coverage/uniform active replay index retain useful information in 20% of the active slots without degrading predeclared historical synthetic-development scores?
hypothesis: Using 10 of 50 source-pinned FIT witness references, PCER will preserve Brier within +0.02 versus full 50-row replay on the historical return-to-old-regime held slice, and be no worse than the strongest equally sized replay control. This is exploratory, not a native-science claim.

inputs.name: Amalgam archived synthetic selection-dev-01 trace.json; no new source actions

frozen_design.split: Original archive order: FIT indices [0,50), VALID [50,64), RETURN_HELD [64,96). Do not shuffle or inspect labels for fitting. Held is historical familiar regime return, NOT unfamiliar world/family transfer.
frozen_design.ordering: Read original canonical trace without modification. Select only FIT; evaluate exactly once on untouched ordered VALID/RETURN_HELD. No hyperparameter selection.
frozen_design.data_budget: Existing 96 already-consumed synthetic episodes; 0 new source actions; FIT 50, VALID 14, RETURN_HELD 32
frozen_design.compute_budget: Four beta-Bernoulli cell estimators each fit at most 50 rows; 2 scored slices totaling 46 rows each; at most 2000 paired bootstrap resamples per seed; no gradient model training, no GPU, no protected actions
frozen_design.capacity: PCER 10 references: 7 error priority, 2 rare coverage, 1 deterministic uniform. Uniform and pure error each 10 references; full-history control 50. Original full source remains immutable outside active index. 80% active-slot reduction is not checkpoint/total-bytes reduction.
frozen_design.evaluator: For each chosen row, context=(views[0][0],row.x1); transition target=row.s2; fully fit beta-Bernoulli posterior p=(ones+1)/(n+2) with prior Beta(1,1); mean (p-y)^2 Brier on 14 VALID and 32 RETURN_HELD. Surrogate diagnostic only, no native learner update.

selection: For every FIT row compute prequential surprise (prediction.native / 1e6 - row.s2)^2; sort descending surprise, break ties ascending identifier. Error arm top 7. From remaining choose coverage arm 2 by rarest (context, first action) frequency in FIT, ties by identifier ascending. From remaining choose 1 uniform deterministically by sha256('PCER-01|24011|'+id) ascending. Pure error top 10. Uniform top 10 by same digest. IDs unique. Fail closed on bad source hash, malformed records, duplicate identifier, nonfinite scores, leakage or budget mismatch.
controls: Full-history all 50 FIT records, same estimator, upper-memory reference
Uniform bounded 10 records, same estimator and FIT visibility
Pure error priority 10 records, same estimator and FIT visibility
metrics: cold selection manifest reproduces exact IDs

classification_rules.supported: Exploratory surrogate support only if active 10/50 (80%) and both VALID and RETURN_HELD PCER Brier <= full-history Brier +0.02 and PCER <= min(uniform10,error10) -0.005; still SCIENTIFIC_UNVERIFIED for native learner. Native SCIENTIFIC_PASS additionally requires prospective untouched source-native cohorts, >=3 independent seeds, same-cohort fully trained controls matched in information/actions/compute, cold native restoration, interference/novel transfer gains and independent qualification.
classification_rules.mixed: One Brier guard fails or bounded control tie without source integrity fault => exploratory NO_GO, preserve all outcomes.
classification_rules.negative: Any >+0.02 per-slice Brier regression or failure to beat bounded controls by 0.005 => exploratory NO_GO; classify scientific native gain UNVERIFIED.
classification_rules.invalid: Source SHA mismatch, different dataset/split, leakage, mismatch in capacity, insufficient or duplicated records, missing negative controls, prior outcome inspected before this prereg commit, or hidden evaluator changes.

preregistration_note: Freeze to a new research-only branch before reading/scoring the archived trace outcomes. Entire held test is retrospective exploratory development; never claim new native improvement or scientific promotion.
